page: Microsoft Azure E16ads_v7 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the Eadsv7 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 8 physical AMD EPYC 9V45 cores with hyper-threading, operating at a clock speed of 4.5 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. The processor includes a 32 MB L3 cache, 1.0 MB L2 cache, and 48 KB L1d cache, alongside advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512 (including VNNI and BF16) and cryptography acceleration via AES and SHA_NI.

This instance is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per core. It includes 945 GB of local storage and supports Premium Storage. In benchmark testing, the server demonstrates top-tier single-core performance, scoring in the top 10% for single-core stress-ng, Geekbench single-core, and single-threaded gzip compression. Multi-core performance, memory bandwidth (51.3 GB/sec read and 34.09 GB/sec write for large uncached blocks), and database operations fall within the average tier.

Given its high memory density and strong single-threaded performance, the E16ads_v7 is highly cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require GPU acceleration. It is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching systems like Redis, text processing, and light LLM inference using smaller models. However, multi-threaded scaling and large-model LLM inference represent performance tradeoffs, as these workloads perform in the average to weak ranges.

Built on the x86_64 architecture under Microsoft Hyper-V, it features 128.0 GB of RAM and 945 GB of local storage with Premium Storage capabilities. The server exhibits top-tier single-core CPU performance and single-threaded compression speeds, while multi-core operations and memory bandwidth remain in the average tier. Lacking a GPU, it is designed for memory-intensive, non-accelerated workloads. The high memory-to-vCPU ratio makes it a highly efficient choice for database operations, in-memory caching, text processing, and small-scale language model inference.
